  - Legumes: Cowpea (*Vigna unguiculata*), Groundnut (*Arachis hypogaea*), Soybean (*Glycine max*). High protein, fix atmospheric nitrogen via root nodules (*Rhizobium*).
  - Roots & Tubers: Cassava (*Manihot esculenta*), Yam (*Dioscorea* spp.), Sweet potato (*Ipomoea batatas*). Propagated vegetatively.
  - Beverage & Cash Crops: Cocoa (*Theobroma cacao*), Oil Palm (*Elaeis guineensis*), Rubber (*Hevea brasiliensis*), Cotton (*Gossypium* spp.).
- **Cultural Practices in Crop Production:**
  - *Pre-Planting:* Site selection, clearing, stumping, plowing, harrowing, ridging, seed treatment (dressing with fungicides/insecticides).
  - *Planting:* Direct seeding vs. nursery bed transplanting (cocoa, oil palm, tomato, pepper, citrus); seed rate, planting depth, plant spacing.
  - *Post-Planting:*
    - **Thinning:** Removing excess weak seedlings from a stand to leave the vigorous ones.
    - **Supplying:** Replanting empty stands where seeds failed to germinate.
    - **Mulching:** Covering soil surface with dry plant materials to conserve moisture, suppress weeds, and regulate temperature.
    - **Staking:** Providing bamboo/wooden sticks to support climbing crops (yam, tomato) for sunlight exposure.
    - **Pruning:** Selective removal of unproductive branches or diseased shoots.

---

topics.title: Weeds, Crop Pests, and Diseases
topics.content:
- **Weeds:** Any plant growing where it is not desired, competing with crops for light, nutrients, water, and space. Examples: Spear grass (*Imperata cylindrica*), Siam weed (*Chromolaena odorata*), Guinea grass (*Panicum maximum*), Witchweed (*Striga hermonthica* - parasitic on cereals).
- **Crop Pests:**
  - *Biting and Chewing:* Locusts, grasshoppers, armyworms, variegated grasshopper (*Zonocerus variegatus*), beetles. Destroy leaf foliage. Controlled by stomach poisons.
  - *Piercing and Sucking:* Aphids, cotton stainer (*Dysdercus* spp.), cocoa mirids/capsids (*Sahlbergella singularis*), green spider mite. Pierce tissues, suck sap, and transmit viral diseases. Controlled by **systemic insecticides**.
  - *Boring Pests:* Maize stem borer (*Busseola fusca*), bean weevil (*Callosobruchus maculatus*), rice weevil (*Sitophilus oryzae*). Bore into stems and stored grains. Controlled by fumigants.
- **Important Crop Diseases:**
  | Crop Disease | Causal Organism Type | Specific Pathogen / Vector | Diagnostic Symptoms & Control |
  | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
  | **Black Pod of Cocoa** | Fungus | *Phytophthora palmivora* | Brown/black water-soaked lesions on pods; controlled by spraying **copper sulfate (Bordeaux mixture)** and frequent harvesting. |
  | **Cassava Mosaic Disease (CMD)** | Virus | Cassava Mosaic Virus (Vector: **Whitefly, *Bemisia tabaci*)** | Mottled, chlorotic, distorted leaves, stunted plants; controlled by planting resistant cuttings and rogueing infected plants. |
  | **Cocoa Swollen Shoot** | Virus | Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus (Vector: **Mealybug, *Pseudococcus*)** | Swelling of twigs and roots, red vein-banding on leaves; controlled by cutting out and burning infected trees. |
  | **Maize Smut** | Fungus | *Ustilago maydis* | Large black gall-like fungal growths filled with dark sooty spores on cobs and tassels. |
  | **Groundnut Rosette** | Virus | Groundnut Rosette Virus (Vector: **Aphid, *Aphis craccivora*)** | Chlorotic, stunted, bushy rosette foliage; controlled by early planting at close spacing to deter aphids. |

---

# SECTION 3: ANIMAL SCIENCE, NUTRITION & VETERINARY HEALTH

topics.title: Anatomy and Digestive Physiology of Farm Animals
topics.content:
- **Ruminants (Polygastric: Cattle, Sheep, Goats):**
  - Stomach divided into **4 distinct chambers**:
    1. **Rumen (Paunch):** First and largest compartment; lined with papillae; contains billions of symbiotic micro-organisms (bacteria and protozoa) that produce **cellulase** to digest cellulose/fiber; synthesizes Vitamin B-complex and amino acids. Food is fermented and later regurgitated.
    2. **Reticulum (Honeycomb):** Second chamber with honeycomb-like mucosal folds; collects heavy foreign objects (wire, nails) to prevent hardware disease; aids regurgitation of cud into mouth for chewing.
    3. **Omasum (Manyplies / Bible):** Third chamber filled with leaf-like muscular leaves; absorbs water, volatile fatty acids, and bicarbonate from the digesta.
    4. **Abomasum (True Stomach):** Fourth chamber; only compartment with glandular mucosal lining; secretes **gastric juice (pepsin and $\text{HCl}$)** for true chemical and enzymatic digestion of proteins and microbes.
- **Non-Ruminants (Monogastric: Pigs, Rabbits):** Single simple stomach. Rabbits practice **Coprophagy / Caecotrophy** (ingesting soft nighttime fecal pellets directly from anus to absorb microbial vitamins produced in the large caecum).
- **Poultry Digestive System:**
  - *Beak:* Captures feed; no teeth (cannot chew).
  - *Crop:* Muscular pouch at base of esophagus for temporary storage, softening, and lubrication of feed.
  - *Proventriculus (Glandular Stomach):* Secretes digestive enzymes (pepsin) and $\text{HCl}$.
  - *Gizzard (Ventriculus):* Thick, heavily muscled organ lined with a tough koilin membrane; contains swallowed **grit and small stones** that grind hard seeds and grains into a fine paste.
  - *Cloaca:* Common chamber for digestive, urinary, and reproductive tracts opening to the vent.

---

topics.title: Animal Nutrition and Feeding Practices
topics.content:
- **Types of Rations:**
  - **Maintenance Ration:** Minimum quantity of balanced feed required to sustain the animal's basal metabolic functions and keep body weight constant without performing work or yielding production.
  - **Production Ration:** Extra balanced feed supplied **over and above maintenance requirements** to support economic output: growth/fattening, milk production (lactation), egg laying, wool growth, or foetal development during late pregnancy (**steaming up**).
- **Feed Classifications:**
  - *Roughages:* High fiber ($>18\%$), low Total Digestible Nutrients (TDN); e.g., pasture grasses (*Elephant grass, Guinea grass*), legumes (*Centrosema, Stylosanthes*), **Hay** (dried forage grass, moisture $<15\%$), **Silage** (succulent forage preserved by anaerobic fermentation in a silo).
  - *Concentrates:* Low fiber ($<18\%$), high TDN; e.g., Basal/Energy feeds (maize, sorghum, cassava meal) and Protein concentrates (soybean meal, groundnut cake - GNC, fishmeal, bloodmeal).
  - *Additives:* Bone meal (calcium/phosphorus), oyster shell, salt licks, vitamins, antibiotics.

---

topics.title: Livestock Diseases and Parasites
topics.content:
- **Viral Diseases:**
  - **Rinderpest (Cattle Plague):** Severe fever, bloody diarrhea, necrotic sores on mucous membranes; controlled by rinderpest vaccination.
  - **Newcastle Disease (Poultry):** Viral infection characterized by respiratory distress, nervous symptoms (**twisted neck / torticollis**), paralysis, and **greenish diarrhea**; high mortality; controlled by Newcastle vaccine (NDV-i2 / Lasota).
  - **Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD):** Blisters on tongue, lips, and hooves in cloven-hoofed cattle/swine; severe salivation and lameness.
  - **Gumboro (Infectious Bursal Disease):** Attacks the bursa of Fabricius in young chicks, destroying their immune system.
- **Bacterial Diseases:**
  - **Anthrax (*Bacillus anthracis*):** Peracute zoonotic disease; causes sudden death with **dark, tarry, uncoagulated blood oozing from all natural body orifices (mouth, nose, anus)**; rigor mortis is incomplete; **carcass must never be opened/autopsied** (spores are extremely resistant and fatal to humans); bury deeply in quicklime.
  - **Brucellosis (Contagious Abortion - *Brucella abortus*):** Causes late-term abortion (5th–8th month) in pregnant cows, retained placenta, and infertility; zoonotic (causes Undulant fever in humans via raw unpasteurized milk).
- **Protozoan Diseases & Parasites:**
  - **Trypanosomiasis (Nagana in cattle):** Caused by *Trypanosoma* spp., transmitted by the **Tsetse fly (*Glossina*)**; causes intermittent fever, progressive emaciation, dullness, anemia, and death. Muturu and N'Dama cattle are trypano-tolerant.
  - **Coccidiosis (Poultry & Calves):** Caused by *Eimeria* spp.; causes droopiness, ruffled feathers, and **bloody diarrhea**; controlled by anticoccidial drugs (Amprolium, Sulfa drugs) and dry litter.
  - **Liver Fluke (*Fasciola hepatica*):** Flatworm parasite inhabiting bile ducts of sheep and cattle, causing liver rot; requires the freshwater **mud snail (*Lymnaea*)** as its essential intermediate host.
  - **Tapeworm (*Taenia solium* in pigs, *Taenia saginata* in cattle):** Primary host is human (intestines); intermediate host is pig/cow (bladder worms/cysticercus in muscle meat).

---

# SECTION 4: AGRICULTURAL ECONOMICS, RECORDS & MECHANIZATION

topics.title: Agricultural Economics & Farm Records
topics.content:
- **Farm Records & Accounts:**
  - *Farm Inventory:* A complete list of all assets on the farm with their physical descriptions and monetary values at a specific date.
  - *Production Record:* Details daily agricultural output (liters of milk, crates of eggs, bags of grain harvested).
  - *Farm Budget:* Forward-looking estimate of total expected farm revenue and expenses for a future production period (Complete budget vs. Partial budget).
  - *Balance Sheet / Net Worth Statement:*
    $$\text{Net Worth (Owner's Equity)} = \text{Total Assets} - \text{Total Liabilities}$$
- **Agricultural Marketing:**
  - Marketing channels: Producer $\to$ Commission Agent $\to$ Wholesaler $\to$ Retailer $\to$ Consumer.
  - Functions: Assembling, processing, grading/standardization, packaging, storage, transportation, financing, and risk-bearing.

---

topics.title: Farm Mechanization & Surveying
topics.content:
- **Primary vs. Secondary Tillage Implements:**
  - *Primary Tillage (Ploughing):* Deep inversion, cutting, and shattering of hard soil.
    - **Disc Plough:** Fitted with rotating concave steel discs; ideal for rough, hard, stony, root-infested tropical soils; rolls over obstacles without breaking.
    - **Mouldboard Plough:** Inverts and turns over soil completely, burying weeds; suitable for loose, weed-free, stone-free soils.
  - *Secondary Tillage (Harrowing & Ridging):* Breaking down clods, leveling seedbeds, and shaping soil.
    - **Disc Harrow:** Pulverizes soil clods into fine tilth after ploughing.
    - **Ridger:** Gathers loose soil into ridges and furrows for root crop planting (cassava, yam, sweet potato).
- **Farm Surveying Instruments:**
  - *Gunter's Chain:* Measuring distances; exactly **66 feet long (20.12 meters)**, composed of **100 wire links** connected by rings (each link $= 7.92\text{ inches} = 0.66\text{ ft}$).
  - *Arrows (Survey Pins):* Steel pins used to mark the end of each chain length measured.
  - *Ranging Poles:* Wooden or metal poles painted in alternating red and white bands, used for marking stations and aligning straight survey lines.
  - *Prismatic Compass:* Measures magnetic bearings and angles.

---

name: Geography
overview:
**Subject Code:** `GEO`  
**Total Questions in UTME:** 40 Questions  
**Time Target:** 25 – 27 Minutes  
**Maximum Scaled Score:** 100 Marks  
**Authoritative Reference:** Official JAMB IBASS Syllabus for Geography  

---

## Overview & How JAMB Tests Geography

In the UTME, Geography is tested via **40 multiple-choice questions** grouped into four major areas:
1. **Practical Geography & Cartography (~8 Questions):** Map scales, scale reduction and enlargement, distance and area measurement, bearing, contour interpretation, slope and gradient calculation, cross-sections, intervisibility, and drainage patterns.
2. **Physical Geography & Geomorphology (~16 Questions):** Earth's rotation and revolution, longitudinal local time calculations, earth's interior structure, rock classification, landform development (fluvial, desert, karst, coastal, glacial), vulcanicity, planetary winds, and climatic zones.
3. **Human & Economic Geography (~8 Questions):** Population distribution, demographic factors, rural/urban settlements, world agricultural systems, mineral and energy resources, transportation, and industrialization.
4. **Regional Geography of Nigeria (~8 Questions):** Physical background (relief, drainage, river systems), climate (monsoon vs. harmattan air masses), vegetation zones, agriculture, mineral distribution (petroleum, coal, tin, iron ore), and major environmental hazards.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Guaranteed Calculations in JAMB Geography:**
> - Local Time & Longitude: The earth rotates $360^\circ$ in 24 hours $\implies 15^\circ = 1\text{ hour} \implies 1^\circ = 4\text{ minutes}$. Moving East $\to$ **Add time (+)**; Moving West $\to$ **Subtract time (-)**.
> - Scale Reduction/Enlargement: When a map is reduced by half, the Representative Fraction (RF) denominator is **doubled** ($1:50,000 \to 1:100,000$). When enlarged by 2, the denominator is **halved** ($1:50,000 \to 1:25,000$).
> - Gradient Calculation: $\text{Gradient} = \frac{\text{Vertical Interval (VI)}}{\text{Horizontal Equivalent (HE)}}$.

---

# SECTION 1: PRACTICAL GEOGRAPHY AND MAPWORK

strategies.title: Strategy 1
strategies.description: **Local Time Golden Rule (EGA / WLS):** **East Gain Add; West Lose Subtract**. Find the degree difference first ($15^\circ = 1\text{ hr}, 1^\circ = 4\text{ mins}$). If destination is East of reference meridian, ADD time; if West, SUBTRACT.

strategies.title: Strategy 2
strategies.description: **Back Bearing Shortcut:** If forward bearing is $< 180^\circ$, **ADD $180^\circ$**. If forward bearing is $> 180^\circ$, **SUBTRACT $180^\circ$**. E.g., Back bearing of $045^\circ = 45 + 180 = 225^\circ$.

strategies.title: Strategy 3
strategies.description: **Scale Reduction/Enlargement Area Rule:** If a map scale is reduced by half ($2$), its area becomes $\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{4}$ of the original. If enlarged by $3$, area becomes $3^2 = 9$ times larger!

strategies.title: Strategy 4
strategies.description: **Stalactite vs Stalagmite Mnemonic:** Stala**C**tite has **C** for Ceiling (hangs down); Stala**G**mite has **G** for Ground (grows up from floor).

strategies.title: Strategy 5
strategies.description: **V-Contour Rule for Rivers:** Contour V-lines point **UPSTREAM (uphill)** towards the river source. A river always flows in the direction the V opens (downhill).

strategies.title: Strategy 6
strategies.description: **Highest Mountain Peak in Nigeria:** The highest point in Nigeria is **Chappal Waddi ($2,419\text{ m}$)** on the Shebshi Mountains in Taraba State, NOT Shere Hills in Jos ($1,829\text{ m}$).

strategies.title: Strategy 7
strategies.description: **Lapse Rate Calculation:** For every $1,000\text{ meters}$ rise, temperature drops by $6.5^\circ\text{C}$. If sea level is $30^\circ\text{C}$, at $2,000\text{ meters}$ altitude temperature will be $30 - (2 \times 6.5) = 17^\circ\text{C}$.

strategies.title: Strategy 8
strategies.description: **Radial Drainage on Jos Plateau:** Rivers radiating outward in all directions from the center indicate a **Radial Drainage Pattern** (characteristic of the Jos Plateau).

strategies.title: Strategy 9
strategies.description: **Metamorphic Rock Equivalents:** Limestone becomes **Marble**; Sandstone becomes **Quartzite**; Shale becomes **Slate**; Granite becomes **Gneiss**.

strategies.title: Strategy 10
strategies.description: **Trellis vs Dendritic Patterns:** Dendritic is tree-like on uniform rock. Trellis has tributaries joining the main river at **$90^\circ$ right angles** on alternating hard and soft rocks.

topics.title: Map Scales and Measurements
topics.content:
- **Types of Scales:**
  - *Statement Scale:* Expressed in words (e.g., "$1\text{ cm}$ represents $1\text{ km}$").
  - *Representative Fraction (RF):* Ratio of map distance to ground distance in the same unit (e.g., $1:50,000$, meaning $1\text{ cm}$ on the map represents $50,000\text{ cm} = 500\text{ m} = 0.5\text{ km}$ on the ground).
  - *Linear (Graphic) Scale:* A divided bar drawn at the bottom of the map.
- **Conversion Example:**
  - Convert $1:50,000$ to a statement scale:
    $$50,000\text{ cm} \div 100,000\text{ cm/km} = 0.5\text{ km} \implies 2\text{ cm represents } 1\text{ km}$$
- **Scale Reduction & Enlargement Rules:**
  - *Reduction:* When a map is reduced by a factor of $n$, multiply the old RF denominator by $n$.
    $$\text{Example: Reduce a } 1:50,000 \text{ map by half } (2) \implies 1:(50,000 \times 2) = 1:100,000$$
    *(Map area becomes } \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{4} \text{ of the original area)*.
  - *Enlargement:* When a map is enlarged by a factor of $n$, divide the old RF denominator by $n$.
    $$\text{Example: Enlarge a } 1:50,000 \text{ map by } 2 \implies 1:(50,000 \div 2) = 1:25,000$$
- **Bearings & Direction:**
  - *Fore Bearing:* The clockwise angle measured from True North ($000^\circ - 360^\circ$).
  - *Back Bearing:*
    - If Fore Bearing $< 180^\circ \implies \text{Back Bearing} = \text{Fore Bearing} + 180^\circ$.
    - If Fore Bearing $> 180^\circ \implies \text{Back Bearing} = \text{Fore Bearing} - 180^\circ$.

---

topics.title: Relief Representation and Map Interpretation
topics.content:
- **Contours:** Lines on a map connecting points of equal height above mean sea level. The vertical distance between two successive contour lines is the **Vertical Interval (VI)**.
  - *Steep Slope:* Contours are drawn **very close together**.
  - *Gentle Slope:* Contours are drawn **widely spaced apart**.
  - *Uniform Slope:* Contours are **evenly spaced**.
  - *Concave Slope:* Closely packed contours at the top, widely spaced at the bottom.
  - *Convex Slope:* Widely spaced contours at the top, closely packed at the bottom.
  - *Cliff:* Contours merge or touch one another.
  - *Spur vs. Valley:*
    - **Spur:** Contour V-shapes point towards **lower ground** (downhill).
    - **Valley:** Contour V-shapes point towards **higher ground** (uphill / upstream).
- **Gradient Calculation:**
  $$\text{Gradient} = \frac{\text{Vertical Interval (VI)}}{\text{Horizontal Equivalent (HE)}}$$
  *(Ensure VI and HE are converted into the SAME unit before dividing! Express as a ratio, e.g., $1\text{ in } 25$)*.
- **Intervisibility:** Two points are intervisible if an observer at point A can see an observer at point B without an intervening hill or ridge blocking the line of sight. Checked by constructing a relief cross-section.
- **Drainage Patterns:**
  - *Dendritic:* Resembles the branches of a tree; develops on rocks of uniform resistance.
  - *Trellis:* Tributaries join the main river at approximately **right angles ($90^\circ$)**; develops in areas of alternating parallel bands of hard and soft rocks.
  - *Radial:* Rivers flow outward in all directions from a central elevated dome or volcanic cone (e.g., Jos Plateau).
  - *Centripetal:* Streams flow inward from surrounding highlands into a central depression or inland drainage basin (e.g., Lake Chad basin).

---

# SECTION 2: PHYSICAL GEOGRAPHY AND GEOMORPHOLOGY

topics.title: Earth Movements, Longitudes and Time
topics.content:
- **Earth's Rotation (Every 24 Hours on its axis, tilted at $23.5^\circ$):**
  - Causes Day and Night, creates deflection of winds and ocean currents (Coriolis effect), causes sunrise and sunset, and produces the daily cycle of tides.
- **Earth's Revolution (Every $365\frac{1}{4}$ days around the Sun):**
  - Causes the Four Seasons (Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter), varying lengths of day and night throughout the year, and changes in the altitude of the midday sun.
  - **Equinoxes (March 21 & September 23):** Midday sun is overhead at the Equator; equal day and night ($12\text{ hours}$ each) worldwide.
  - **Summer Solstice (June 21):** Sun is overhead at the Tropic of Cancer ($23.5^\circ\text{N}$); longest day in Northern Hemisphere.
  - **Winter Solstice (December 22):** Sun is overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn ($23.5^\circ\text{S}$); longest night in Northern Hemisphere.
- **Local Time & Longitude Calculations:**
  - Rate: $360^\circ = 24\text{ hours} \implies 15^\circ = 1\text{ hour} \implies 1^\circ = 4\text{ minutes}$.
  - Rule: **East Gain Add (EGA), West Lose Subtract (WLS)**.
  - *Worked Example:* If local time at Greenwich ($0^\circ$) is 12:00 noon, what is the local time in a town on Longitude $45^\circ\text{E}$?
    $$\text{Difference in longitude} = 45^\circ - 0^\circ = 45^\circ$$
    $$\text{Time difference} = \frac{45^\circ}{15^\circ/\text{hr}} = 3\text{ hours}$$
    $$\text{Since town is East of Greenwich } \to 12:00 + 3\text{ hours} = \mathbf{3:00\text{ PM}}$$

---

topics.title: Earth's Interior and Rock Classification
topics.content:
- **Internal Layers of the Earth:**
  - *Crust (Lithosphere):* Solid outer layer ($0-40\text{ km}$). Continental crust (**Sial:** Silica + Aluminium, lighter, granite) and Oceanic crust (**Sima:** Silica + Magnesium, denser, basalt). Separated from mantle by the **Mohorovičić Discontinuity (Moho)**.
  - *Mantle (Mesosphere):* Semi-molten plastic rock ($40-2,900\text{ km}$), rich in olivine. Separated from core by the **Gutenberg Discontinuity**.
  - *Core (Barysphere / Centrosphere):* Deepest layer ($2,900-6,370\text{ km}$); composed of **Nife** (Nickel + Iron). Outer core is liquid; inner core is solid due to immense pressure.
- **Classification of Rocks:**
  1. **Igneous Rocks:** Formed by the cooling and solidification of molten magma/lava. Crystalline, non-stratified, contain no fossils.
     - *Plutonic (Intrusive):* Cooled slowly deep underground; coarse-grained crystals (e.g., **Granite, Gabbro, Diorite**).
     - *Volcanic (Extrusive):* Cooled rapidly on earth's surface; fine-grained crystals (e.g., **Basalt, Obsidian, Pumice**).
  2. **Sedimentary Rocks:** Formed from accumulation and lithification of sediments in layers (strata); contain fossils.
     - *Mechanically formed:* Sandstone, Shale, Clay, Conglomerate.
     - *Organically formed:* Formed from remains of living organisms (Limestone, Chalk, Coral, Coal).
     - *Chemically formed:* Formed by precipitation from solutions (Rock salt, Gypsum, Potash).
  3. **Metamorphic Rocks:** Pre-existing rocks completely altered by immense heat and pressure:
     - Limestone $\to$ **Marble**
     - Sandstone $\to$ **Quartzite**
     - Shale $\to$ **Slate**
     - Granite $\to$ **Gneiss**
     - Coal $\to$ **Graphite / Diamond**

---

topics.title: Landform Development and Geomorphic Processes
topics.content:
- **Fluvial (River) Landforms Across 3 Stages:**
  - *Youth / Upper Course (Dominant process: Vertical erosion):* V-shaped valleys, interlocking spurs, gorges, canyons, waterfalls, rapids, and river capture.
  - *Mature / Middle Course (Dominant process: Lateral erosion & transportation):* U-shaped valleys, meanders, river cliffs, and slip-off slopes.
  - *Old Age / Lower Course (Dominant process: Deposition):* Ox-bow lakes, natural levees, deferred tributaries, floodplains, braided channels, and **deltas** (Arcuate e.g. Niger/Nile; Bird's foot e.g. Mississippi; Estuarine e.g. Congo/Rhein).
- **Desert (Wind & Water) Landforms:**
  - *Wind Erosion Landforms:* **Zeugen** (ridge of alternating horizontal hard/soft rock), **Yardang** (vertically striped rocks), **Rock Pedestal / Mushroom Rock**, **Inselberg** (steep-sided isolated residual hill), **Deflation Hollow** (creates oases when reaching water table).
  - *Wind Deposition Landforms:* **Barchan** (crescent-shaped sand dune with horns pointing downwind), **Seif Dunes** (longitudinal ridges parallel to wind), **Loess** (fine wind-blown dust).
  - *Water Action in Deserts:* **Wadis** (dry desert gullies), **Bajada**, **Playa** (ephemeral salt lake).
- **Karst (Limestone) Landforms:**
  - Formed by chemical dissolution of calcium carbonate by carbonated rainwater:
    $$\text{CaCO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2 \rightleftharpoons \text{Ca(HCO}_3)_2 \quad (\text{Soluble Calcium Bicarbonate})$$
  - Surface features: Grikes and Clints (limestone pavements), Sinkholes / Swallow holes, Dolines, Uvalas, Poljes.
  - Underground features: Caves/caverns; **Stalactites** (calcite deposits hanging down from cave roof; "C" for ceiling); **Stalagmites** (calcite pillars growing up from cave floor; "G" for ground); **Pillar** (stalactite and stalagmite joining).
- **Coastal Landforms:**
  - *Erosional Features:* Headlands and bays, sea cliffs, wave-cut platforms, sea caves, **arches, stacks, and stumps** (sequential erosion of headland).
  - *Depositional Features:* Beaches, sand spits, baymouth bars, **tombolos** (sand ridge connecting an island to the mainland).

---

topics.title: Weather, Climate, and Planetary Winds
topics.content:
- **Weather Instruments & The Stevenson Screen:**
  - *Stevenson Screen:* White-painted, double-louvered wooden box on four legs, $1.21\text{ meters}$ above ground; houses **Maximum and Minimum Thermometer (Six's)** and **Hygrometer (Wet and Dry bulb thermometer)** to protect from direct sun and precipitation while allowing free air circulation.
  - *Other Instruments:* Rain Gauge (rainfall, sited in open ground away from trees), Mercury Barometer (atmospheric pressure), Anemometer (wind speed in knots), Wind Vane (wind direction).
- **Lapse Rate:** The rate of temperature decrease with altitude. Normal environmental lapse rate $= \mathbf{6.5^\circ\text{C}\text{ per } 1,000\text{ meters}}$ (or $1^\circ\text{C}$ per $160\text{ meters}$).
- **Planetary Winds & Pressure Belts:**
  - Doldrums (Equatorial Low Pressure Belt: $0^\circ - 5^\circ\text{N/S}$).
  - Horse Latitudes (Sub-Tropical High Pressure Belts: $30^\circ\text{N/S}$).
  - ITCZ (Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone): Oscillating low-pressure trough where trade winds converge.

---

# SECTION 3: REGIONAL GEOGRAPHY OF NIGERIA

topics.title: Physical Geography of Nigeria
topics.content:
- **Location & Extent:** Located entirely within the tropics in West Africa between Latitudes **$4^\circ\text{N}$ and $14^\circ\text{N}$**, and Longitudes **$3^\circ\text{E}$ and $15^\circ\text{E}$**.
- **Relief Regions of Nigeria:**
  - *Highlands ($>300\text{ meters}$):*
    - **Jos Plateau:** North-central granitic plateau; radial drainage hub; highest point is Shere Hills ($1,829\text{ m}$).
    - **Northern High Plains:** Undulating landscape of crystalline basement rocks (Hausaland).
    - **Western Highlands:** Inselberg-studded granite ranges of Yoruba uplands (Idanre hills).
    - **Eastern Highlands:** Mountainous border with Cameroon; contains **Chappal Waddi ($2,419\text{ meters}$)** in Taraba State — the **highest mountain peak in Nigeria**.
  - *Lowlands ($<300\text{ meters}$):* Sokoto plains, Chad basin, Niger-Benue trough, Coastal plains, and Niger Delta.
- **Drainage of Nigeria:**
  - Dominated by River Niger (enters Nigeria from Niger Republic, third longest river in Africa) and River Benue (enters from Cameroon), joining at the **Lokoja Confluence** to form a single trunk river emptying into the Atlantic via the Niger Delta.
  - **Radial Drainage Hub:** The **Jos Plateau** acts as the primary hydrographic center from which rivers flow in all directions (River Kaduna and Gongola to Niger/Benue; Rivers Hadejia and Jama'are to Lake Chad).

---

topics.title: Climate, Vegetation, and Resources of Nigeria
topics.content:
- **The Two Air Masses Influencing Nigerian Weather:**
  1. **Tropical Maritime Air Mass (mT / South-West Monsoon Wind):** Originates over the South Atlantic Ocean; warm and moisture-laden; brings the **Rainy Season** across Nigeria (heavy rainfall in the south, decreasing northward).
  2. **Tropical Continental Air Mass (cT / North-East Trade Wind):** Originates over the Sahara Desert; dry, cold, and dust-laden; brings the **Harmattan / Dry Season** across Nigeria (peaks from November to February).
- **Vegetation Belts of Nigeria (South to North):**
  1. *Mangrove Swamp Forest:* Tidal coastal creeks, brackish water; red mangrove (*Rhizophora*) with stilt roots and white mangrove (*Avicennia*) with breathing roots (pneumatophores).
  2. *Freshwater Swamp Forest:* Permanent freshwater swamps in the delta; raffia palms.
  3. *Tropical Rainforest:* High rainfall ($>2,000\text{ mm}$), tall hardwood timber trees with layered canopies, buttress roots, lianas, and epiphytes (Iroko, Mahogany, Obeche).
  4. *Southern Guinea Savanna:* Tall grasses, fire-resistant trees; broad transition zone.
  5. *Northern Guinea Savanna:* Moderately tall grasses, open woodland (Isoberlinia).
  6. *Sudan Savanna:* Short feathery grasses, thorny acacia, baobab trees with bulbous water-storing trunks.
  7. *Sahel Savanna:* Semi-arid desert border, sparse drought-resistant tussock grasses and date palms.
- **Mineral Resources Distribution in Nigeria:**
  - **Petroleum & Natural Gas:** Niger Delta (Rivers, Bayelsa, Delta, Akwa Ibom, Ondo, Imo, Abia).
  - **Coal:** Sub-bituminous coal at **Enugu** (Udi hills) and Kogi.
  - **Tin & Columbite:** Alluvial deposits on the **Jos Plateau** (Bukuru).
  - **Iron Ore:** **Itakpe** and Agbaja in Kogi State (supplies Ajaokuta and Aladja steel complexes).
  - **Limestone:** Used for cement manufacturing in **Ewekoro/Sagamu** (Ogun), **Gboko** (Benue), **Nkalagu** (Ebonyi), **Ashaka** (Gombe), **Sokoto**.
  - **Lead and Zinc:** Found together at **Abakaliki** (Ebonyi) and Zurak (Plateau).

---

name: History
overview:
**Subject Code:** `HIS`  
**Total Questions in UTME:** 40 Questions  
**Time Target:** 25 – 27 Minutes  
**Maximum Scaled Score:** 100 Marks  
**Authoritative Reference:** Official JAMB IBASS Syllabus for History  

---

## Overview & How JAMB Tests History

In the UTME, History is tested via **40 multiple-choice questions** grouped into four major chronological segments:
1. **Nigeria up to 1800 (~10 Questions):** Early archaeological civilizations (Nok, Ife, Benin, Igbo-Ukwu), Kanem-Borno, the Hausa States (Bayajidda legend), the Old Oyo Empire, Nupe, Jukun, and the Trans-Saharan Trade.
2. **19th-Century Transformations (~10 Questions):** The 1804 Sokoto Islamic Jihad (Usman Dan Fodio), Kanem-Borno under al-Kanemi, the Yoruba Civil Wars (Owu and Kiriji wars), European explorers (Mungo Park, Lander Brothers), and Christian missionary enterprises.
3. **Colonial Rule, Indirect Rule & Nationalism (1900–1960) (~12 Questions):** British military conquests, the 1914 Amalgamation by Lord Lugard, Indirect Rule across Northern, Western, and Eastern regions, early nationalist movements, political parties (NNDP, NYM, NCNC, AG, NPC, NEPU), and constitutional milestones.
4. **Post-Independence Politics & Wider Africa (~8 Questions):** The First Republic, military coups of 1966, the Nigerian Civil War (1967–1970), the oil boom, the Berlin Conference (1884–1885), the Scramble for Africa, Apartheid in South Africa, and regional bodies (AU, ECOWAS).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Key Exam Chronologies in JAMB History:**
> - **1804:** Outbreak of the Sokoto Jihad led by Shaykh Usman Dan Fodio.
> - **1830:** The Lander Brothers (Richard and John) discover the mouth of the River Niger emptying into the Bight of Benin.
> - **1851 / 1861:** British bombardment of Lagos (1851) and formal annexation of Lagos as a Crown Colony under King Dosunmu (1861).
> - **1884–1885:** Berlin West Africa Conference partitions Africa among European imperial powers.
> - **1886 / 1893:** Peace treaty ending the 16-year Kiriji / Ekiti-Parapo War in Yorubaland.
> - **January 1, 1914:** Lord Frederick Lugard amalgamates the Northern and Southern Protectorates with the Colony of Lagos.
> - **May 30, 1967 – January 15, 1970:** The Nigerian Civil War.

---

# SECTION 1: NIGERIA UP TO 1800 (EARLY CIVILIZATIONS)

strategies.title: Strategy 1
strategies.description: **Bernard Fagg and the Nok Culture:** Whenever a question asks who excavated or scientifically recognized the **Nok Culture**, the answer is **Bernard Fagg** (1943).

strategies.title: Strategy 2
strategies.description: **First African Anglican Bishop:** **Bishop Samuel Ajayi Crowther** was consecrated as the first African bishop in 1864 and translated the Bible into Yoruba.

strategies.title: Strategy 3
strategies.description: **Thurstan Shaw and Igbo-Ukwu:** The archaeological excavations of the 9th-century bronze roped pot and Eze Nri artifacts at Igbo-Ukwu were carried out by **Thurstan Shaw**.

strategies.title: Strategy 4
strategies.description: **Motive for the 1914 Amalgamation:** Lord Lugard amalgamated Nigeria in 1914 strictly for **financial/economic convenience**—using Southern customs revenue surpluses to subsidize Northern administrative deficits.

strategies.title: Strategy 5
strategies.description: **Herbert Macaulay's Moniker:** Herbert Macaulay is universally recognized as the **"Father of Nigerian Nationalism"** and founded the first political party in Nigeria (NNDP, 1923).

strategies.title: Strategy 6
strategies.description: **Kiriji War Duration and Treaty:** The Kiriji / Ekiti-Parapo War lasted for **16 years (1877–1893)** and was resolved by the Peace Treaty of 1886/1893.

strategies.title: Strategy 7
strategies.description: **Biafra Surrender Date:** The Nigerian Civil War officially ended on **January 15, 1970**, when General Philip Effiong surrendered to General Yakubu Gowon.

strategies.title: Strategy 8
strategies.description: **Otto von Bismarck and Berlin:** The 1884–1885 Berlin West Africa Conference that partitioned Africa was convened by German Chancellor **Otto von Bismarck**.

strategies.title: Strategy 9
strategies.description: **FESTAC '77 Symbol:** The official emblem of the 1977 Second World Black and African Festival of Arts and Culture (FESTAC) was the **16th-century Ivory Mask of Queen Mother Idia of Benin**.

strategies.title: Strategy 10
strategies.description: **Sokoto Jihad 1804 Battle:** The decisive initial battle of the 1804 Sokoto Jihad was the **Battle of Tabkin Kwatto** (June 1804).

topics.title: Early Archaeological Cultures in Nigeria
topics.content:
- **The Nok Culture (c. 900 BC – 200 AD):**
  - Located in the Nok valley of Kaduna State, spreading across Jos Plateau and Benue valley.
  - Discovered in 1928 by tin miners and excavated scientifically by British archaeologist **Bernard Fagg** in 1943.
  - Recognized for producing the **oldest terracotta sculptures in Sub-Saharan Africa**, distinguished by pierced triangular/oval eyes, flaring nostrils, and elaborate hairstyles.
  - Proved early knowledge of **iron smelting** in West Africa independent of external civilizations.
- **Ile-Ife:**
  - Spiritual and ancestral cradle of the Yoruba people; tradition attributes its founding to **Oduduwa**.
  - Renowned for naturalistic bronze/brass and terracotta portrait heads produced via the **cire-perdue (lost-wax) casting technique**, depicting divine kings (**Ooni**) and royal consorts with facial scarifications.
- **The Benin Kingdom:**
  - Founded by the Ogiso dynasty (Sky Kings); later transformed when Prince Oranmiyan of Ife arrived and established the Oba dynasty, fathering **Oba Eweka I**.
  - **Oba Ewuare the Great (15th Century):** Expanded the empire, fortified the city with monumental defensive earthworks (Benin City walls and moats), and established royal guilds.
  - Famous royal brass-casting guild (**Iguneronmwon**) produced ceremonial plaques, commemorative heads, and the famous **Ivory Mask of Queen Mother Idia** (adopted as the official symbol of the Second World Black and African Festival of Arts and Culture — **FESTAC '77**).
  - Destroyed during the British Punitive Expedition of February 1897 under Admiral Harry Rawson; Oba Ovonramwen was exiled to Calabar, and thousands of royal bronze artifacts were plundered.
- **Igbo-Ukwu (9th Century AD):**
  - Located in Anambra State; accidentally discovered in 1938 by **Isaiah Anozie** while digging a water cistern; excavated by British archaeologist **Thurstan Shaw** in 1959.
  - Unearthed hundreds of leaded bronze castings decorated with intricate floral, geometric, and filigree motifs (e.g., the bronze roped pot), alongside over 165,000 glass trade beads and a sacred burial chamber of an **Eze Nri** (priest-king of the ancient Nri Kingdom).

---

topics.title: Northern Kingdoms and the Trans-Saharan Trade
topics.content:
- **Kanem-Borno Empire:**
  - Founded around Lake Chad by the nomadic Kanuri under the **Sayfawa Dynasty** (one of the longest-ruling dynasties in world history, c. 850 – 1846 AD).
  - Initial capital at **Njimi** (east of Lake Chad); relocated to **Birni Ngazargamu** in the late 15th century by Mai Ali Gaji.
  - **Mai Idris Alooma (1571–1603):** Brought Kanem-Borno to its Golden Age; instituted Islamic legal reforms, introduced Turkish military instructors, imported muskets/firearms from the Ottoman Empire, and organized a formidable camel cavalry.
- **The Hausa States (Hausa Bakwai & Banza Bakwai):**
  - **The Bayajidda Legend:** Prince Abuyazidu (Bayajidda) fled Baghdad, arrived in Daura, killed the sacred snake *Sarki* that prevented the townsfolk from drawing water, and married the Queen of Daura (**Daurama**).
  - *Hausa Bakwai (The 7 Legitimate States):* Daura, Kano, Katsina, Zaria (Zazzau), Gobir, Rano, and Biram.
  - *Banza Bakwai (The 7 Illegitimate / Bastard States):* Kebbi, Zamfara, Nupe, Gwari, Yauri, Ilorin, and Kwararafa.
  - Specializations: Kano and Katsina (commerce and dye-pits), Zaria (warriors and slave supply), Gobir (northern defensive bastion against desert nomads).
- **The Trans-Saharan Caravan Trade:**
  - Network of trade routes connecting North Africa and the Mediterranean coast with the West African forest and savanna regions across the Sahara Desert.
  - *Goods Exported from West Africa:* Gold, slaves, ivory, ostrich feathers, dyed leather (Moroccan leather), and **kola nuts**.
  - *Goods Imported into West Africa:* Rock salt, cowrie shells (currency), horses, firearms, textiles, brassware, and glass beads.
  - Major Northern Nigerian termini: **Kano, Katsina, and Kukawa**.

---

# SECTION 2: 19TH-CENTURY TRANSFORMATIONS IN NIGERIA

topics.title: The 1804 Sokoto Islamic Jihad
topics.content:
- **Leader:** **Shaykh Usman Dan Fodio** (1754–1817), a learned Fulani Islamic scholar and preacher of the Toronkawa clan, assisted by his brother **Abdullahi Dan Fodio** and his son **Muhammad Bello**.
- **Underlying Causes:**
  - *Religious:* Corruption and syncretism of local Hausa rulers who mixed Islamic practices with traditional pagan animism (*shirk*).
  - *Social and Political:* Oppression and corruption of the Habe rulers of Gobir (Sarki Nafata and Sarki Yunfa), arbitrary justice, and moral decadence.
  - *Economic:* Imposition of heavy, un-Islamic taxes (**Jangali** on cattle, market tolls, extortionate land taxes) which infuriated Fulani pastoralists and peasant Hausa farmers (**Talakawa**).
- **Outbreak & Spread:**
  - Sarki Yunfa attempted to assassinate Usman Dan Fodio and attacked his community at Degel.
  - Usman Dan Fodio performed **Hijra** (flight) from Degel to Gudu on February 21, 1804; his followers declared him **Amir al-Mu'minin** (Commander of the Faithful).
  - Decisive victory at the **Battle of Tabkin Kwatto (June 1804)** against the royal army of Gobir.
- **Establishment & Structure of the Sokoto Caliphate:**
  - Replaced corrupt Hausa Habe rulers with Fulani Emirs across Katsina, Kano, Zaria, Adamawa, Bauchi, Nupe, and Ilorin.
  - Divided administratively in 1812:
    - **Western Sector (Gwandu):** Administered by brother **Abdullahi Dan Fodio**.
    - **Eastern Sector (Sokoto):** Administered by son **Muhammad Bello** (who became the second Sultan of Sokoto).
- **Kanem-Borno's Defense:**
  - Borno successfully repelled the Fulani jihadist invasions through the military and religious leadership of **Muhammad al-Amin al-Kanemi**, an Islamic scholar from Kanem who challenged Dan Fodio's religious justifications in written theological letters. Al-Kanemi displaced the ancient Sayfawa dynasty and established the **Shehu Dynasty** with its new capital at **Kukawa**.

---

topics.title: The Yoruba Civil Wars and the Fall of Old Oyo
topics.content:
- **Collapse of the Old Oyo Empire:**
  - Internal constitutional crises between the **Alaafin (Aole)** and his **Bashorun**; imperial army overextended.
  - **Afonja's Rebellion (1817):** Afonja, the Are-Ona-Kakanfo based at **Ilorin**, revolted against Alaafin Aole, allied with Fulani Muslim elements led by **Shehu Alimi**, and broke away from Oyo. Alimi's followers later assassinated Afonja, absorbing Ilorin into the Sokoto Caliphate as a Fulani emirate under Emir Abdulsalami.
  - Fulani cavalry sacked the imperial capital **Oyo-Ile (Katunga)** around 1835; Alaafin Atiba founded a new capital at present-day Oyo.
- **The Yoruba Wars of the 19th Century:**
  - *The Owu War (1821–1826):* Sparked by a dispute at the Apomu market; Allied forces of Ife and Ijebu laid a 5-year siege on fortified **Owu**, completely leveling it. Generated hundreds of thousands of refugees, triggering massive population shifts.
  - *Rise of New Military Centers:*
    - **Ibadan:** Founded in 1829 as a joint military camp of Oyo, Ife, and Ijebu warriors; evolved into a republican military superpower based on individual merit and valor rather than hereditary monarchy.
    - **Abeokuta:** Founded in 1830 by Egba refugees led by **Sodeke** under the protective outcrop of Olumo Rock.
    - **Ijaye:** Led by military general **Kurunmi**, champion of conservative Oyo tradition.
  - *The 16-Year Kiriji / Ekiti-Parapo War (1877–1893):*
    - The longest civil war in Yoruba history.
    - Triggered by Ibadan's oppressive imperial rule, extortionate tax collectors (**Ajeles**), and military arrogance.
    - The eastern Yoruba states formed the **Ekiti-Parapo Grand Alliance** led by **Fabunmi of Imesi-Ile** and Commander-in-Chief **Ogedengbe of Ilesha**, fighting Ibadan troops under **Latosa**.
    - Ended through British diplomatic and military intervention with the **Peace Treaty of 1886** and final pacification of Yorubaland in **1893**.

---

topics.title: European Exploration and Christian Missions
topics.content:
- **Exploration of the River Niger:**
  - **Mungo Park:** Scottish explorer; dispatched by the African Association. In his first journey (1795–1797), he reached the Niger at Segou and proved it flows **eastward**. In his second journey (1805), he drowned with his companions at the **Bussa Rapids** in modern Niger State.
  - **Hugh Clapperton, Dixon Denham, and Walter Oudney (1822–1824):** Crossed Sahara; discovered Lake Chad; Clapperton visited Kano, Sokoto, and Sultan Muhammad Bello.
  - **The Lander Brothers (Richard and John Lander, 1830):** Solved the long-standing geographic mystery of the Niger's termination; sailed down the river from Bussa and proved it empties into the Atlantic Ocean through the vast maze of creeks in the **Niger Delta (Oil Rivers)**.
- **Christian Missionary Endeavors:**
  - Led by freed African returnees from Sierra Leone (Saro) and European societies: Church Missionary Society (CMS), Roman Catholic Mission (RCM), Methodists, and Presbyterians.
  - **Bishop Samuel Ajayi Crowther (CMS):** Captured as a boy from Osogun in Yorubaland, rescued by the British naval squadron, educated in Sierra Leone and England. Accompanied the 1841 Niger Expedition; consecrated the **first African Anglican Bishop** in 1864 at Canterbury Cathedral; **translated the Holy Bible and Anglican Book of Common Prayer into the Yoruba language**.
  - **Mary Slessor (Presbyterian Church of Scotland):** Arrived in Calabar in 1876; successfully campaigned against the barbaric traditional practice of **killing twin babies** and human sacrifices among the Efik and Ibibio peoples.

---

# SECTION 3: COLONIAL RULE, NATIONALISM & INDEPENDENCE (1900–1960)

topics.title: British Conquest and the 1914 Amalgamation
topics.content:
- **British Territorial Acquisition:**
  - 1851: Bombardment of Lagos (deposed King Kosoko, installed King Akitoye).
  - 1861: Annexation of Lagos as a British Crown Colony by Treaty signed with King Dosunmu.
  - 1885: British declared the **Oil Rivers Protectorate** (later Niger Coast Protectorate) following the Berlin Conference.
  - Subjugation of Indigenous Resistance:
    - **King Jaja of Opobo:** Resisted British commercial monopoly in palm oil; tricked aboard HMS *Goshawk* by Consul Harry Johnston in 1887 and exiled to Saint Vincent in the West Indies.
    - **Nana Olomu of Itsekiri:** Resisted British intrusion; British bombarded his heavily defended capital at Ebrohimi in 1894; exiled to the Gold Coast.
    - **The 1897 British Punitive Expedition on Benin:** Oba Ovonramwen exiled to Calabar.
    - **Conquest of Northern Nigeria (1900–1903):** Led by Sir Frederick Lugard; British forces took Kano and Sokoto; Sultan Attahiru I was martyred at the Battle of Burmi (1903).
- **The Amalgamation of January 1, 1914:**
  - **Sir Frederick Lugard** unified the **Protectorate of Northern Nigeria** and the **Protectorate of Southern Nigeria** (along with the Colony of Lagos) into a single political entity: **The Colony and Protectorate of Nigeria**.
  - *Primary Motive:* Financial expediency. The Northern Protectorate operated under constant budget deficits subsidized by imperial grants, while the Southern Protectorate enjoyed vast customs revenue surpluses from maritime trade and spirits imports. Lugard amalgamated both to use the Southern financial surplus to balance Northern deficits and fund railway construction.

---

topics.title: The Nationalist Movement & Political Parties
topics.content:
- **Pioneering Nationalism (Herbert Macaulay Era):**
  - **Herbert Macaulay (1864–1946):** Grandson of Bishop Ajayi Crowther; surveyor, civil engineer, journalist, and politician; widely revered as the **"Father of Nigerian Nationalism"**.
  - Founded the **Nigerian National Democratic Party (NNDP)** in 1923 following the introduction of the elective principle under the Clifford Constitution; dominated the 3 elected seats for Lagos from 1923 to 1938.
- **The Nigerian Youth Movement (NYM, 1934):**
  - Formed by energetic educated youths: **Ernest Ikoli, Dr. J.C. Vaughan, Kofo Abayomi, H.O. Davies**, joined later by **Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe** (1937) and **Chief Obafemi Awolowo**.
  - First genuine pan-Nigerian nationalist movement with branches across the nation; broke the NNDP's monopoly by winning all Lagos seats in the 1938 Legislative Council elections. Disintegrated in 1941 due to ethnic factionalism during the vacant legislative council seat contest between Ernest Ikoli and Samuel Akinsanya.
- **The Tripartite Regional Parties (1950s):**
  - **NCNC (National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons):** Founded in 1944 with Herbert Macaulay as President and Nnamdi Azikiwe as General Secretary. Mainstream party in the Eastern Region and parts of the Western Region.
  - **Action Group (AG):** Founded in 1951 by **Chief Obafemi Awolowo** as the political wing of the Yoruba cultural organization, *Egbe Omo Oduduwa*. Slogan: "Life More Abundant"; introduced **free universal primary education**, modern healthcare, and Africa's first television station (WNTV, 1959) in the Western Region.
  - **Northern People's Congress (NPC):** Evolved from the cultural group *Jam'iyyar Mutanen Arewa*; dominated by the Northern traditional aristocracy; led by **Sir Ahmadu Bello (Sardauna of Sokoto)** and **Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa**. Slogan: "One North, One People, Irrespective of Religion, Rank or Tribe".
  - **NEPU (Northern Elements Progressive Union):** Radical, populist opposition party in the North founded in 1950 by **Mallam Aminu Kano**; championed the rights of the commoners (*Talakawa*) against feudal aristocratic exploitation.

---

# SECTION 4: POST-INDEPENDENCE NIGERIA & WIDER AFRICA

topics.title: Post-Independence Politics & The Civil War (1960–1970)
topics.content:
- **The First Republic (1960–1966):** Prime Minister was Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa (NPC); ceremonial President was Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe (NCNC).
- **The First Military Coup (January 15, 1966):**
  - Executed by young military officers led by **Major Chukwuma Kaduna Nzeogwu** and Major Emmanuel Ifeajuna.
  - Assassinated Prime Minister Balewa, Northern Premier Ahmadu Bello, Western Premier Ladoke Akintola, and Federal Finance Minister Festus Okotie-Eboh.
  - **Major-General J.T.U. Aguiyi-Ironsi** assumed power; issued **Unification Decree No. 34** in May 1966 abolishing the federal system; sparked northern anti-Ironsi riots.
- **The Counter-Coup (July 29, 1966) & Road to War:**
  - Ironsi was assassinated at Ibadan by northern counter-coup plotters; **Lt. Col. Yakubu Gowon** became Head of State and restored federalism.
  - Severe anti-Igbo pogroms in the North prompted millions of Easterners to flee to their homeland.
  - **The Aburi Accord (January 1967):** Meeting held in Aburi, Ghana, hosted by General Joseph Ankrah, between Gowon and Eastern Region Military Governor **Lt. Col. Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu** to preserve peace. Differing interpretations of the agreement led to deadlock.
  - Gowon restructured Nigeria into **12 states on May 27, 1967** to break regional hegemony.
  - On **May 30, 1967**, Ojukwu formally proclaimed the Eastern Region as the independent **Republic of Biafra**.
- **The Nigerian Civil War (July 6, 1967 – January 15, 1970):**
  - Fighting broke out at Garkem on July 6, 1967.
  - Federal troops enforced a complete naval and economic blockade around Biafra, leading to catastrophic mass starvation and kwashiorkor.
  - Biafra surrendered unconditionally on **January 15, 1970** when Major-General Philip Effiong delivered the instrument of surrender to General Gowon at Dodan Barracks, Lagos.
  - Gowon declared: **"No victor, no vanquished"**, launching the national policy of the **3Rs (Reconciliation, Rehabilitation, and Reconstruction)**.

---

topics.title: Wider Africa and Global Affairs
topics.content:
- **The Scramble for Africa & Berlin Conference (1884–1885):**
  - Convened by German Chancellor **Otto von Bismarck** in Berlin to avoid military conflict among European powers over African territory.
  - Enacted the **Doctrine of Effective Occupation** (a European power had to formally occupy and demonstrate administrative control over an African territory before claiming sovereignty). Ignored indigenous ethnic boundaries, dividing ethnic groups across artificial colonial frontiers.
- **The Apartheid Regime in South Africa (1948–1994):**
  - Institutionalized racial segregation introduced by the Afrikaner-dominated National Party in 1948, forcing non-white South Africans into impoverished reserves (**Bantustans / Homelands**).
  - Tragic milestones: **Sharpeville Massacre (1960)**, Soweto Youth Uprising (1976).
  - Anti-Apartheid heroes: **Nelson Mandela, Oliver Tambo, Walter Sisulu, Steve Biko** (founder of Black Consciousness Movement), and Archbishop Desmond Tutu.
  - Nigeria's Leading Role: Despite geographic distance, Nigeria was officially designated a **"Frontline State"**; boycotted the 1976 Montreal Olympics over New Zealand's rugby tour of South Africa, nationalized assets of Barclays Bank and British Petroleum (BP) to pressure Britain, and established the South Africa Relief Fund (SARF).
  - Mandela was released in February 1990 after 27 years imprisonment; universal non-racial democratic elections held on **April 27, 1994** elected Nelson Mandela as South Africa's first black President.

---

name: Christian Religious Studies
overview:
**Subject Code:** `CRK` / `CRS`  
**Total Questions in UTME:** 40 Questions  
**Time Target:** 25 – 27 Minutes  
**Maximum Scaled Score:** 100 Marks  
**Authoritative Reference:** Official JAMB IBASS Syllabus for Christian Religious Studies  

---

## Overview & How JAMB Tests CRS

In the UTME, Christian Religious Studies is tested via **40 multiple-choice questions** grouped into three canonical areas:
1. **Themes from the Old Testament (~14 Questions):** Sovereignty of God, Creation, the Fall, covenants (Abraham, Moses), judges, kings of Israel (Saul, David, Solomon), division of the kingdom, prophetic ministries (Elijah, Amos, Hosea, Isaiah), and the exile and return.
2. **Themes from the Gospels & the Acts of the Apostles (~16 Questions):** Birth and early life of Jesus, baptism and temptations, the Sermon on the Mount, parables and miracles, passion, crucifixion, resurrection, Pentecost, life of the early church, martyrdom of Stephen, Philip's ministry, Paul's conversion, Peter and Cornelius, and the Jerusalem Council (Acts 15).
3. **Themes from Selected Epistles (~10 Questions):** Pauline theology (Justification by Faith in Romans, Law and Grace in Galatians, Spiritual Gifts and Love in 1 Corinthians, Humility in Philippians, Civic submission in Romans 13), Faith and Works (James), and the Parousia (1 Thessalonians).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Key Exam Characteristics for JAMB CRS:**
> - Questions test **precise biblical names, relationships, and locations** (e.g., Mount Carmel for Elijah's contest; Mount Gilboa where Saul died; Joppa where Peter raised Dorcas and had his vision; Lystra where Paul and Barnabas were called Hermes and Zeus).
> - Specific prophetic analogies must be identified (e.g., Hosea's unfaithful wife **Gomer** as a symbol of Israel's spiritual adultery; Amos' condemnation of the wealthy women of Samaria as **"cows of Bashan"**).

---

# SECTION 1: THEMES FROM THE OLD TESTAMENT

strategies.title: Strategy 1
strategies.description: **Jerusalem Council Verdict (Acts 15):** The council decided that Gentile converts do **NOT** need circumcision, but must abstain from idols, blood, strangled meat, and sexual immorality.

strategies.title: Strategy 2
strategies.description: **Prophetic Marital Metaphors:** **Hosea's** marriage to the adulterous **Gomer** symbolizes God's enduring love for unfaithful Israel.

strategies.title: Strategy 3
strategies.description: **Amos' Target Audience:** Amos prophesied primarily against the social corruption, economic injustice, and fraudulent scales of **Northern Israel (Samaria)**, even though he was born in Tekoa (Judah).

strategies.title: Strategy 4
strategies.description: **Mount Carmel vs Mount Sinai:** The contest between Elijah and the 450 prophets of Baal took place on **Mount Carmel**; the 10 Commandments were given to Moses on **Mount Sinai (Horeb)**.

strategies.title: Strategy 5
strategies.description: **Stephen's Dying Words:** Stephen cried: *"Lord, do not charge them with this sin"* and *"Lord Jesus, receive my spirit"*, reflecting Christ's words on the cross.

strategies.title: Strategy 6
strategies.description: **Simon the Sorcerer (Simony):** The sin of attempting to buy the power and gifts of the Holy Spirit with money is called **Simony** (from Simon Magus in Acts 8).

strategies.title: Strategy 7
strategies.description: **Justification Paradigm:** In both Romans and Galatians, Apostle Paul cites **Abraham** as the supreme Old Testament proof that justification is by faith alone, before circumcision.

strategies.title: Strategy 8
strategies.description: **Parables of Lost Things:** Luke 15 contains three parables of lost things: The Lost Sheep, the Lost Coin, and the Lost (Prodigal) Son.

strategies.title: Strategy 9
strategies.description: **First Christian Martyr:** **Stephen** was the first Christian martyr, stoned to death under the supervision of Saul of Tarsus.

strategies.title: Strategy 10
strategies.description: **Saul's Disobedience at Gilgal and Amalek:** King Saul was rejected as king for two specific sins: offering sacrifice without Samuel at Gilgal, and sparing King Agag and the best livestock of Amalek.

topics.title: Sovereignty of God, Creation, and Covenant
topics.content:
- **The Two Creation Accounts:**
  - *Genesis 1 (Priestly account):* Creation by divine spoken word in six days; God creates man (male and female) on the sixth day in His image; rests on the seventh day (Sabbath). Order: Light $\to$ Firmament $\to$ Seas/Dry land/Plants $\to$ Sun/Moon/Stars $\to$ Fish/Birds $\to$ Land animals/Man.
  - *Genesis 2 (Yahwist account):* Man formed from the dust of the ground, God breathes the breath of life into his nostrils; God plants the Garden of Eden; woman created from man's rib.
- **The Fall of Man (Genesis 3):** Disobedience prompted by the serpent's deceit; eating from the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil. Consequences: Serpent condemned to crawl on belly; woman suffers pain in childbirth and submission to husband; man toils to eat from the cursed ground; spiritual death and expulsion from Eden.
- **The Abrahamic Covenant (Genesis 12 & 17):**
  - God's call at Haran (age 75): promises land, descendants, great nation, and universal blessing.
  - Sign of the Covenant: **Circumcision** of every male child at **8 days old**.
  - Ultimate test of faith: Command to sacrifice Isaac on Mount Moriah; God provides a ram caught in a thicket (**Jehovah-Jireh** — The Lord will provide).
- **Moses and the Exodus:**
  - Divine encounter at the Burning Bush on Mount Horeb (**Yahweh** — "I AM WHO I AM").
  - The 10 Plagues on Egypt (concluding with the death of the firstborn).
  - **The Passover Feast (Pesach):** Unblemished yearling lamb/goat, blood smeared on doorposts/lintels, eaten roasted with bitter herbs and unleavened bread, dressed ready for flight.
  - Crossing the Red Sea; God's wilderness provision of Manna and Quail; Water from the rock at Rephidim (Massah and Meribah).
  - The Sinai Covenant: The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) given on two stone tablets on Mount Sinai.

---

topics.title: Leadership and Kingship in Israel
topics.content:
- **The Judges of Israel:**
  - *Deborah:* Prophetess and judge; sat under the Palm of Deborah; commanded **Barak** to lead Israel's army against Jabin's general **Sisera**; Sisera fled and was killed by **Jael** with a tent peg through his temple.
  - *Gideon:* Called while threshing wheat in a winepress; destroyed father's Baal altar; defeated the Midianite army using only **300 men** armed with trumpets, torches, and pitchers.
  - *Samson:* Nazarite from birth (vow: no razor on head, no wine, no touching dead bodies); supernatural strength; betrayed by **Delilah** of the Valley of Sorek who cut his seven locks of hair.
- **Eli and Samuel:**
  - Eli the High Priest at Shiloh; failed to restrain his wicked sons (**Hophni and Phinehas**) who desecrated sacrificial offerings and committed immorality at the tabernacle; judgment pronounced through young boy Samuel; Eli dies falling from his seat on hearing the Ark of God was captured by Philistines.
- **The Monarchy: Saul, David, and Solomon:**
  - *Saul:* First King of Israel; anointed by Samuel. Disobedience: offered premature burnt sacrifice at Gilgal without Samuel; spared King Agag and the best sheep/cattle of the Amalekites. Samuel's rebuke: *"To obey is better than sacrifice, and to heed than the fat of rams."*
  - *David:* Anointed at Bethlehem; played harp to soothe Saul's tormenting spirit; killed Goliath with a sling and smooth stone; covenant of friendship with **Jonathan**; committed adultery with **Bathsheba** and orchestrated the murder of her husband **Uriah the Hittite**; confronted by Prophet **Nathan** with the parable of the rich man and the ewe lamb; repented (Psalm 51).
  - *Solomon:* Given wisdom, wealth, and honor after offering 1,000 burnt offerings at Gibeon; built the first Temple in Jerusalem; downfall caused by marrying 700 foreign wives and 300 concubines who turned his heart to idolatry (Ashtoreth, Chemosh, Molech).
  - *Division of the Kingdom (931 BC):* Solomon's son **Rehoboam** rejected the advice of the elders and adopted the harsh advice of young men ("My father scourged you with whips, but I will scourge you with scorpions"); ten northern tribes broke away under **Jeroboam I** to form the Northern Kingdom of Israel (capital: Samaria); southern kingdom became Judah (capital: Jerusalem).

---

topics.title: Prophetic Ministries and Religious Reforms
topics.content:
- **Elijah on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18):**
  - Confronted King Ahab and Queen Jezebel over Baal worship.
  - Contest on Mount Carmel: Elijah vs. 450 prophets of Baal. Baal prophets prayed, danced, and cut themselves without answer; Elijah rebuilt the altar of the Lord with 12 stones, poured 12 jars of water, prayed a simple prayer, and fire fell from heaven consuming the sacrifice, wood, stones, and water; people cried: *"The Lord, He is God!"*; Baal prophets slaughtered at the Brook Kishon.
  - Naboth's Vineyard: Jezebel framed Naboth with false witnesses and had him stoned to death so Ahab could seize his vineyard; Elijah pronounced divine judgment on Ahab and Jezebel.
- **Prophetic Messages of Social Justice:**
  - *Amos:* Shepherd from Tekoa in Judah sent to prophesy in Northern Israel (Samaria). Condemned greed, luxury, bribery, cheating with false weights and measures, selling the righteous for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals; denounced wealthy women as *"cows of Bashan"*; declared that external religious rituals are worthless without righteousness: *"Let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream."*
  - *Hosea:* Commanded to marry an unfaithful woman (**Gomer**) to illustrate God's unceasing covenant love and mercy toward unfaithful Israel.
  - *Josiah's Reforms (2 Kings 22–23):* King Josiah ordered repairs on the Temple; High Priest **Hilkiah** discovered the **Book of the Law**; verified by Prophetess **Huldah**; Josiah tore his clothes, destroyed all pagan altars and high places, defiled Topheth, and reinstituted the Passover feast.

---

# SECTION 2: THE GOSPELS AND THE ACTS OF THE APOSTLES

topics.title: Life and Ministry of Jesus Christ
topics.content:
- **Birth and Early Life:**
  - Annunciation to Mary by Angel Gabriel; born in Bethlehem; visited by shepherds and Magi (Wise Men bearing gold, frankincense, myrrh); dedication in the temple recognized by **Simeon** (*Nunc Dimittis*) and prophetess **Anna**; escape to Egypt to evade Herod's slaughter of innocents; Jesus at age 12 in the temple debating with Jewish doctors of the law.
- **Baptism and Temptations:**
  - Baptized by John the Baptist in the Jordan River; the Holy Spirit descended like a dove, and a voice from heaven declared: *"This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."*
  - Fasted 40 days and nights in the wilderness; tempted by Satan in three areas:
    1. *Stones to bread* (Fleshly appetite) $\to$ "Man shall not live by bread alone..."
    2. *Throwing Himself from temple pinnacle* (Presumption / Testing God) $\to$ "You shall not tempt the Lord your God."
    3. *Worshiping Satan for kingdoms of the world* (Idolatry / Power) $\to$ "You shall worship the Lord your God, and Him only shall you serve."
- **The Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5–7):**
  - The Beatitudes: Spiritual blessings for the poor in spirit, meek, merciful, peacemakers, and persecuted.
  - Metaphors of disciples: "Salt of the earth" and "Light of the world".
  - Moral standards: Anger equated with murder, lustful looking equated with adultery, loving enemies, prayer, fasting in secret, storing treasures in heaven, and the Golden Rule (*"Do unto others as you would have them do unto you"*).
- **Parables and Miracles:**
  - *Parables of the Kingdom:* The Sower (four soils: path, rocky, thorns, good soil); Wheat and Tares; Mustard Seed; Prodigal Son (unconditional fatherly forgiveness); Good Samaritan (defining who is my neighbor: priest and Levite pass by, Samaritan shows mercy).
  - *Categories of Miracles:*
    - Nature: Water turned to wine at Cana (first miracle); calming the storm; feeding the 5,000 with 5 barley loaves and 2 small fish.
    - Healing: The paralytic lowered through the roof; the woman with the issue of blood for 12 years; ten lepers (only the Samaritan returned to give thanks); blind Bartimaeus at Jericho.
    - Resurrection: Jairus' daughter; the widow's son at Nain; Lazarus raised after four days in the tomb.
- **Passion, Crucifixion, and Resurrection:**
  - Triumphal Entry into Jerusalem on a donkey (Palm Sunday); cleansing of the temple.
  - The Last Supper: Institute of Holy Communion (bread = broken body, wine = new covenant in blood).
  - Agony in the Garden of Gethsemane (*"Not my will, but yours be done"*); betrayed with a kiss by **Judas Iscariot** for 30 pieces of silver; arrested; denied three times by Peter before the cock crowed.
  - Trials: Before the Sanhedrin (Caiaphas), Pontius Pilate, and Herod Antipas; crowd demanded the release of **Barabbas** and the crucifixion of Jesus.
  - Crucifixion at Golgotha (The Place of a Skull); Simon of Cyrene compelled to carry the cross; died on Good Friday; buried in the rock-hewn tomb of **Joseph of Arimathea**.
  - Resurrection on Sunday morning; discovered empty by Mary Magdalene; Great Commission on the mountain in Galilee; Ascension into heaven from the Mount of Olives.

---

topics.title: The Early Church and the Acts of the Apostles
topics.content:
- **The Day of Pentecost (Acts 2):**
  - 120 disciples gathered in the Upper Room; sudden sound of a rushing mighty wind; cloven tongues like of fire rested on each; filled with the Holy Spirit and began speaking in other tongues; Peter's powerful sermon explaining Joel's prophecy; **about 3,000 souls converted and baptized**.
- **Life in the Early Christian Community:**
  - Devoted to the apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayers; had all things in common; sold possessions to distribute to those in need (Barnabas sold a field); judgment on **Ananias and Sapphira** who lied to the Holy Spirit about the sale price of their land and fell dead.
- **Early Persecution and Expansion:**
  - Appointment of seven deacons to oversee welfare (Stephen, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, Nicolaus).
  - **Stephen:** Arrested for preaching; delivered a magnificent historical defense before the Sanhedrin; saw heaven open and Jesus standing at God's right hand; stoned to death becoming the **first Christian martyr**; young Saul of Tarsus consented to his death.
  - **Philip:** Preached with signs in Samaria; Simon the sorcerer offered money to buy the power of the Holy Spirit (**Simony**); guided by an angel to the Gaza road to preach to and baptize the **Ethiopian Eunuch** who was reading Isaiah 53.
- **Conversion of Saul and Ministry to Gentiles:**
  - Saul blinded by a brilliant light on the road to Damascus (*"Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?"*); sight restored by **Ananias**; transformed into Apostle Paul.
  - **Peter and Cornelius (Acts 10):** Peter saw a vision at Joppa of a sheet descending with clean and unclean animals, commanded: *"What God has cleansed, you must not call common"*; visited the Roman Centurion Cornelius in Caesarea; the Holy Spirit fell upon Gentile listeners; baptized into the Church.
- **The Council of Jerusalem (Acts 15, c. 49 AD):**
  - Convened to resolve whether Gentile converts must be circumcised and obey the Law of Moses to be saved.
  - Peter and Paul testified to God's grace among Gentiles; **James (brother of Jesus)** presided and delivered the apostolic verdict: Gentile Christians were exempt from circumcision, required only to abstain from:
    1. Food sacrificed to idols.
    2. Blood.
    3. Meat of strangled animals.
    4. Sexual immorality.

---

# SECTION 3: THEMES FROM SELECTED EPISTLES

topics.title: Pauline and General Epistles
topics.content:
- **Justification by Faith (Romans 3–5):**
  - All humanity (Jews and Gentiles) has sinned and fallen short of God's glory.
  - Man cannot be justified (declared righteous) before God by the works of the law, but solely by God's free grace through faith in the sacrificial death and resurrection of Jesus Christ.
  - **Abraham** is the ultimate model of justification by faith: he believed God before he was circumcised, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness.
- **Law and Grace (Galatians 3–5):**
  - The Mosaic Law served as a **tutor / schoolmaster** to lead mankind to Christ.
  - Christian liberty: Christians are free from the ceremonial yoke of the law; warn against returning to legalism.
  - Contrast: *Works of the Flesh* (fornication, idolatry, sorcery, anger, drunkenness) vs. *Fruit of the Spirit* (love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control).
- **Spiritual Gifts and the Supremacy of Love (1 Corinthians 12–13):**
  - One body with many diverse members; spiritual gifts distributed by the Spirit for the common good (wisdom, knowledge, faith, healing, miracles, prophecy, tongues).
  - **Chapter 13 (The Hymn of Love):** Without love, the greatest spiritual gifts, eloquent tongues, and sacrificial martyrdom are completely worthless; love is patient, kind, does not envy, never fails; *"Now abide faith, hope, love, these three; but the greatest of these is love."*
- **Humility and Christ's Self-Emptying (Philippians 2):**
  - Disciples commanded to have the mind of Christ who, though being in the form of God, emptied Himself (*kenosis*), took the form of a servant, and became obedient unto death on a cross; wherefore God highly exalted Him and gave Him the name above every other name.
- **Faith and Works (James 1–2):**
  - True faith is active and practical: *"Faith by itself, if it does not have works, is dead."*
  - Condemnation of partiality/discrimination in the church (honoring the wealthy in fine clothes while dishonoring the poor man in filthy rags).
  - Controlling the tongue: Small like a horse's bit or ship's rudder, but can set a whole forest on fire.
- **The Second Coming of Christ / Parousia (1 Thessalonians 4–5):**
  - Reassurance concerning believers who have died ("fallen asleep"); Christ will descend from heaven with a shout, the voice of the archangel, and the trumpet of God; **the dead in Christ will rise first**, then those who are alive will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air. Day of the Lord will come unexpectedly like a thief in the night.

---

name: Islamic Religious Studies
overview:
**Subject Code:** `IRS` / `IS`  
**Total Questions in UTME:** 40 Questions  
**Time Target:** 25 – 27 Minutes  
**Maximum Scaled Score:** 100 Marks  
**Authoritative Reference:** Official JAMB IBASS Syllabus for Islamic Religious Studies  

---

## Overview & How JAMB Tests IRS

In the UTME, Islamic Religious Studies is tested via **40 multiple-choice questions** grouped into three canonical areas:
1. **The Glorious Qur'an & Hadith Sciences (~15 Questions):** History of revelation and compilation, Makkan vs. Madinan Surahs, Tajweed rules, commentary on prescribed Surahs, Hadith terminology (Sanad, Matn, Isnad), the Six Authentic Compilations (*Sihah al-Sittah*), and An-Nawawi's Forty Hadiths.
2. **Tawhid & Jurisprudence / Fiqh (~15 Questions):** Articles of Faith (*Iman*), dimensions of Tawhid, forms of Shirk, the Five Pillars of Islam, purification (*Taharah*), Salah, Zakah rates and recipients, Sawm regulations, Hajj rites, Islamic family law (marriage, divorce, custody), inheritance shares (*Mawarith*), and ethics.
3. **Islamic History & Islam in West Africa (~10 Questions):** Pre-Islamic Arabia (*Jahiliyyah*), biography of Prophet Muhammad (SAW) in Makkah and Madinah, the Rightly Guided Caliphs (*Khulafa' ar-Rashidun*), the spread of Islam to Kanem-Borno, Hausaland, and the 1804 Sokoto Jihad.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Key Legal and Quranic Terminology in JAMB IRS:**
> - The Five Legal Classifications (*Al-Ahkam al-Khamsah*): **Fard/Wajib** (obligatory), **Mustahabb/Sunnah** (recommended), **Mubah** (permissible), **Makruh** (disliked), **Haram** (strictly prohibited).
> - Specific inheritance fractions in the Qur'an: $\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{8}, \frac{2}{3}, \frac{1}{3}, \frac{1}{6}$.
> - Compilation milestones: First compilation under Caliph **Abu Bakr** (compiled by **Zayd ibn Thabit**); standardization and distribution of copies under Caliph **Uthman ibn Affan**.

---

# SECTION 1: THE GLORIOUS QUR'AN AND HADITH SCIENCES

strategies.title: Strategy 1
strategies.description: **Uthmanic Standardization Reason:** Caliph Uthman standardized the Qur'anic text to eliminate differences in dialect and pronunciation among Muslims of non-Arab provinces.

strategies.title: Strategy 2

strategies.description: **Number of Takbirs in Janazah:** The Janazah (funeral) prayer consists of **4 Takbirs** and has **no bowing (Ruku') or prostrations (Sujud)**.
